events.title: FOMC holds rates at 3.75–4.00%, two dissents for a hike
events.why_it_matters: The Fed paused but two dissents for an immediate hike and a statement upgrade to 'strong' economic activity keep a December hike fully priced, tightening financial conditions.
events.what_to_watch: December 8–9 FOMC; whether hawkish dissents grow and how the Fed frames oil-driven inflation.

events.title: US Q3 GDP advance estimate — 3.2% consensus
events.why_it_matters: A 3.2% annualised print would show AI capex and resilient consumption offsetting the oil shock, supporting risk assets but reinforcing the case for a December hike.
events.what_to_watch: Composition: AI investment versus consumer spending; any downside surprise could ease December hike odds.

events.title: US September PCE inflation
events.why_it_matters: PCE is the Fed's preferred gauge; another firm core reading after September CPI at 3.7% y/y would cement December hike expectations.
events.what_to_watch: Core PCE m/m and y/y versus consensus; services supercore stickiness.

events.title: ECB holds deposit rate at 2.50%; December hike priced ~70%
events.why_it_matters: The ECB is caught between a weak economy and energy-driven inflation; a hold with hawkish guidance keeps a December hike on the table and supports the euro.
events.what_to_watch: Lagarde's tone on energy pass-through and the December staff projections.

events.title: Amazon Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: AWS growth and retail margins are the key read on AI monetisation and consumer health after Microsoft and Alphabet; a miss would hit the mega-cap complex.
events.what_to_watch: AWS revenue growth, capex guidance, and advertising momentum.

events.title: China Fifth Plenum concludes — policy communique
events.why_it_matters: The plenum sets the policy framework for the 2027 Party Congress; markets look for signals on stimulus, property support, and technology self-sufficiency.
events.what_to_watch: Communique language on fiscal support, property, and consumption; any new 'quality' growth targets.

events.title: Samsung Q3 2026 earnings — record profit but shares fall 6%
events.why_it_matters: Record AI-memory profit confirms the chip upcycle, but Samsung's cautious capex and margin disappointment contrast with SK Hynix, signalling rotation within semis.
events.what_to_watch: HBM pricing and 2027 capex plans from Samsung and SK Hynix; memory contract negotiations.

events.title: Microsoft Q3 FY2027 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Azure growth and AI capex guidance set the bar for Amazon and Nvidia; a strong print supports the AI infrastructure trade.
events.what_to_watch: Azure constant-currency growth and capex commentary.

events.title: Alphabet Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Google Cloud growth and AI search monetisation are the key tests of whether AI spending is translating into revenue.
events.what_to_watch: Cloud revenue growth, search ad resilience, and capex guidance.

events.title: US midterm elections — Nov 3
events.why_it_matters: A Democratic sweep is not fully priced and could bring higher taxes and regulation; divided government would preserve the status quo but a long count or unrest is a tail risk.
events.what_to_watch: Senate and House control, turnout in key states, and any contested results.

events.title: BOJ holds at 1.25%, likely acknowledges 2% inflation milestone
events.why_it_matters: A hawkish hold with an explicit 2% inflation acknowledgment would cement December hike expectations and support the yen, with global rates spillovers.
events.what_to_watch: Ueda's press conference, vote split, and any change to the inflation outlook language.

events.title: OPEC+ meeting — Nov 1 production decision
events.why_it_matters: With Brent above $110, OPEC+ may face pressure to raise output; a decision to hold would tighten the market further and add to inflation risk.
events.what_to_watch: Saudi-Russia coordination and any signalling on spare capacity.

events.title: Apple Q4 FY2026 earnings — Nov 2
events.why_it_matters: iPhone demand and services growth are the key read on consumer health and the AI hardware cycle; a miss would weigh on the mega-cap complex.
events.what_to_watch: iPhone revenue, Greater China, services margin, and December-quarter guidance.

events.title: US Treasury quarterly refunding announcement — Nov 4
events.why_it_matters: Treasury is expected to cut 20y and 30y auction sizes, which could ease long-end yields but signals fiscal stress; a wildcard for the $31tn Treasury market.
events.what_to_watch: Changes to long-end auction sizes and any shift toward T-bill funding.

events.title: US October jobs report — Nov 6
events.why_it_matters: Consensus is around +80k to +120k; a weak print could ease December hike odds while a strong print would confirm the Fed's hawkish bias.
events.what_to_watch: Nonfarm payrolls, unemployment rate, and average hourly earnings.

events.title: US October CPI — Nov 10
events.why_it_matters: With September CPI at 3.7% y/y and oil above $110, another hot print would all but lock a December hike and pressure long-duration assets.
events.what_to_watch: Headline and core m/m, energy pass-through, and shelter costs.

events.title: Anthropic IPO — mid-November listing window
events.why_it_matters: A blockbuster AI IPO could be a major liquidity event and sentiment marker for the AI trade; unusual lockup terms reduce near-term supply but leave overhang.
events.what_to_watch: Pricing range, demand signals, and whether it crowds out other tech issuance.

events.title: China NBS manufacturing PMI — Oct 31
events.why_it_matters: A sub-50 print would reinforce the two-speed China recovery narrative and keep pressure on Beijing for targeted stimulus.
events.what_to_watch: New orders and export orders sub-indices.

events.title: Eurozone Q3 GDP flash — Oct 30; flash CPI — Nov 4
events.why_it_matters: Weak Q3 growth alongside energy-driven inflation above 3.8% keeps the ECB in a stagflationary bind and supports a December hike.
events.what_to_watch: GDP q/q and HICP core; any sign of energy pass-through to services.

events.title: US ISM Manufacturing (Nov 2) and ISM Services (Nov 4)
events.why_it_matters: Manufacturing has been in contraction for months; services resilience is key to the soft-landing narrative and Fed expectations.
events.what_to_watch: ISM services new orders and employment sub-indices.

events.title: US ADP employment — Nov 4
events.why_it_matters: A leading indicator for Friday's payrolls; a weak ADP print could pull forward rate-cut expectations and weaken the dollar.
events.what_to_watch: Private payrolls and wage growth.

events.title: China Caixin manufacturing PMI — Nov 2
events.why_it_matters: The private survey focuses more on export-oriented SMEs and could diverge from the official NBS PMI.
events.what_to_watch: New export orders and employment.

events.title: South Korea October exports — Nov 1
events.why_it_matters: Semiconductor exports have been surging (first 20 days up 222% y/y); a strong print would confirm the AI-driven chip cycle.
events.what_to_watch: Chip export growth and China-bound shipments.

events.title: ASH 2026 abstracts — Nov 4 (healthcare catalyst)
events.why_it_matters: ASH abstracts are a major catalyst for hematology/biotech stocks; positive data can move small- and mid-cap biotech sharply.
events.what_to_watch: Key abstracts in CAR-T, bispecifics, and sickle-cell disease.

events.title: Japan September core CPI rises to 2.1%, core-core 2.4%
events.why_it_matters: Core inflation exceeded 2% for the first time in nine months, strengthening the case for a December BOJ hike even as the October 30 meeting is expected to hold.
events.what_to_watch: BOJ's inflation forecasts and any shift in yield-curve control.

events.title: Eurozone October flash PMI misses — services 51.7 vs 52.5 expected
events.why_it_matters: Growth momentum slowed in October while input prices accelerated on energy, leaving the ECB caught between a weak economy and 3.8% inflation.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the slowdown extends into Q4 and feeds through to ECB December projections.

events.title: France riots and political crisis after cost-of-living protests
events.why_it_matters: France suffered its worst unrest in years, weakening the government and reinforcing the case for the ECB to hold rather than hike on October 29.
events.what_to_watch: Whether unrest spreads to other EU countries and affects consumer confidence.

events.title: US government funding deadline — Dec 11 (legislative overhang)
events.why_it_matters: The current continuing resolution expires Dec 11; a post-election lame-duck fight over spending and the debt ceiling could trigger a shutdown and market volatility.
events.what_to_watch: Lame-duck session dynamics and Trump's 'veto everything' threat.

events.title: US federal shutdown becomes longest on record; Senate fails 11th funding vote
events.why_it_matters: The shutdown has furloughed roughly 750,000 workers, delayed federal data and is now the longest in US history, raising growth and liquidity risk into the midterms.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the Senate takes up the House stopgap and whether Schumer's split funding/ACA proposal gains Republican support.

events.title: House passes stopgap funding bill; Senate deadlock persists
events.why_it_matters: A House-passed short-term funding measure could end the shutdown if the Senate follows, but the Senate has repeatedly failed to advance spending bills.
events.what_to_watch: Senate procedural votes and whether Trump signs before the November 3 election.

events.title: FOMC holds at 3.75%-4.00%; two dissents for a 25bp hike
events.why_it_matters: The hold was priced, but Cook and Hammack dissenting for a hike keeps a December tightening option alive and steepens the curve.
events.what_to_watch: December fed funds futures, the 10-year yield around 5%, and Warsh's refusal to give forward guidance.

events.title: US Q3 GDP advance and September PCE inflation
events.why_it_matters: Consensus is GDP +3.0% and PCE +3.6% y/y (core +3.1%); a hot core print would harden the December hike case, while a GDP miss would revive growth fears.
events.what_to_watch: Core PCE m/m, services supercore, and the GDP deflator at 8:30 ET.

events.title: October CPI report cancelled because of shutdown data blackout
events.why_it_matters: BLS says it cannot retroactively collect October prices, forcing a first-ever cancellation and triggering TIPS and inflation-derivative fallback mechanisms.
events.what_to_watch: Whether November CPI is also delayed, and how TIPS breakevens and Fed communication adapt to the missing print.

events.title: October jobs report at risk of delay or cancellation
events.why_it_matters: The BLS household survey is vulnerable to the same shutdown collection problems that cancelled October CPI, leaving the Fed without a key input before December.
events.what_to_watch: BLS guidance in the first week of November and any substitute private payroll data.

events.title: ECB holds deposit rate at 2.50%; Lagarde points to December
events.why_it_matters: A hold is fully priced, but Lagarde must balance weak growth, 3.8% inflation and French political risk without pre-committing to December.
events.what_to_watch: Lagarde's language on inflation persistence and any mention of France's bond spread.

events.title: Eurozone October flash CPI and Q3 GDP
events.why_it_matters: Inflation near 3.8% with weak GDP keeps the ECB in a stagflationary bind and complicates the December decision.
events.what_to_watch: Core HICP and services inflation versus the GDP flash.

events.title: Bank of Japan holds at 1.25%; December hike about 80% priced
events.why_it_matters: The hold is expected, but the BoJ is likely to acknowledge 2% underlying inflation for the first time since 2013, cementing a December hike.
events.what_to_watch: Ueda's guidance and the inflation outlook revision; JGB yields and the yen.

events.title: China Fifth Plenum closes; 15th five-year plan communique
events.why_it_matters: The communique will set the 2026-2030 policy framework, with tech self-reliance and 'new quality productive forces' likely prioritised over broad stimulus.
events.what_to_watch: Language on fiscal support, consumption and property; whether the full outline is deferred to the March NPC.

events.title: China October official and Caixin PMIs
events.why_it_matters: PMIs will show whether the export-led chip boom is offsetting weak domestic demand after Q3 GDP beat.
events.what_to_watch: New export orders, production and the official manufacturing PMI versus Caixin.

events.title: China October trade data
events.why_it_matters: Exports were running at +36.3% y/y in September on AI hardware; a slowdown would hit global cyclical sentiment.
events.what_to_watch: Export growth, semiconductor shipments and the bilateral surplus with the US.

events.title: US midterm elections; Congress control at stake
events.why_it_matters: Democrats lead the national generic ballot by about 8 points, and a chamber flip would change the legislative path for taxes, spending and tariffs.
events.what_to_watch: Senate battlegrounds, turnout, and whether a decisive result reduces or prolongs the shutdown.

events.title: Iran rejects US ceasefire draft; Washington prepares post-midterm military options
events.why_it_matters: Iran refused a Qatari-mediated US truce and reportedly said it will not compromise on nuclear issues, while the US has told Gulf states to prepare for action after the midterms.
events.what_to_watch: Any US strike, Iranian retaliation in Hormuz, and Brent's move above $115.

events.title: Hormuz tanker attacks keep Brent near $111-$114
events.why_it_matters: More than a dozen tanker strikes since late September have reduced transit volumes and kept crude above $100, feeding inflation and geopolitical risk premia.
events.what_to_watch: Insurance rates, US naval escorts and whether Iran formally closes the strait.

events.title: Russia signals readiness for trilateral talks with Ukraine and US in November
events.why_it_matters: Moscow says it is ready to resume talks, but both sides continue attacking; any ceasefire would lower energy risk premia.
events.what_to_watch: Whether a trilateral meeting is actually scheduled and whether energy-infrastructure strikes pause.

events.title: OPEC+ November 1 meeting; production unchanged expected
events.why_it_matters: The seven OPEC+ countries already decided to keep September quotas for November, so the meeting is a compliance and forward-guidance event.
events.what_to_watch: Statements on December quotas and whether Hormuz disruptions force a rhetorical response.

events.title: US East/Gulf port strike ongoing; LA/Long Beach watchmen strike set for November 1
events.why_it_matters: About 45,000 ILA dockworkers are already striking at 30+ ports, and roughly 250 ILWU watchmen at the largest US container complex could strike November 1.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the ILWU Local 26 contract extension is extended and whether the ILA talks resume.

events.title: Alphabet Q3 revenue miss; stock falls 10% on AI capex concerns
events.why_it_matters: Alphabet missed revenue and free cash flow fell sharply, reviving doubts about the return on tens of billions of dollars of AI capex.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the selloff spreads to other hyperscalers and whether Amazon's October 29 print stabilises the AI trade.

events.title: Microsoft Q3 beat; Azure grows 48%, capex guidance above $50bn
events.why_it_matters: Azure's 48% growth and heavy but controlled capex reassure that AI demand is monetising, supporting the cloud/semis complex.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Microsoft's capex guide lifts Nvidia, memory and data-centre suppliers.

events.title: Amazon Q3 earnings after the close
events.why_it_matters: AWS growth and retail margins will test whether the AI capex trade can broaden beyond Microsoft after Alphabet's miss.
events.what_to_watch: AWS revenue growth, advertising and 2027 capex commentary.

events.title: Eli Lilly Q3 earnings before the open
events.why_it_matters: Lilly is the GLP-1 bellwether; consensus EPS has fallen sharply, so guidance on obesity-drug supply and pricing matters for the whole healthcare complex.
events.what_to_watch: Mounjaro/Zepbound volumes, 2027 guidance and margin pressure.

events.title: Apple FQ4 earnings; new CEO John Ternus hosts first call
events.why_it_matters: Apple is the largest mega-cap yet to report, and rising memory costs plus the iPhone 18 cycle will set the tone for hardware and suppliers.
events.what_to_watch: Gross margin, iPhone revenue and any commentary on AI monetisation.

events.title: AI/semis earnings week: Palantir, AMD, Qualcomm
events.why_it_matters: Palantir, AMD and Qualcomm give a read on AI software, GPU competition and edge-device demand after the hyperscaler prints.
events.what_to_watch: AMD's data-centre GPU guidance and Qualcomm's handset/auto outlook.

events.title: SK Hynix Q3 operating profit jumps 7x; memory shortage seen through 2030
events.why_it_matters: SK Hynix's record profit and 100 trillion won shareholder return confirm the AI memory super-cycle and tight supply into the next decade.
events.what_to_watch: HBM pricing, Samsung catch-up and memory capex spillover to equipment makers.

events.title: Anthropic files S-1; IPO roadshow expected week of November 9
events.why_it_matters: A record-breaking AI IPO could absorb liquidity and reset valuation benchmarks for private AI assets, with listing targeted for mid-November.
events.what_to_watch: Roadshow pricing, demand from long-only funds and whether the deal crowds out other tech issuance.

events.title: US Treasury quarterly refunding announcement
events.why_it_matters: Bessent's 'Treasury twist' could cut long-bond auction sizes and expand buybacks, a major wildcard for the $31 trillion Treasury market.
events.what_to_watch: 20-year and 30-year auction sizes, buyback guidance and the 10-year yield reaction.

events.title: UK Autumn Budget delivered
events.why_it_matters: Chancellor Healey's first Budget included a £100 energy handout and fuel-duty freeze, relevant for UK consumer and utility names and gilts.
events.what_to_watch: Gilt reaction and whether the fiscal loosening adds to inflation pressure.

events.title: Bank of Canada surprises with 25bp hike to 2.50%
events.why_it_matters: The first hike in over three years signals that high energy prices are broadening into core inflation, a warning for other DM central banks.
events.what_to_watch: Canadian 2-year yields and whether the BoC signals more hikes.

events.title: France political crisis deepens; 10-year OAT yield near 5%
events.why_it_matters: Macron's government is paralysed after the worst unrest in years, with debt at 119% of GDP and the OAT-Bund spread at record highs.
events.what_to_watch: Moody's follow-up, whether a government can pass a budget, and ECB commentary on fragmentation.

events.title: Supreme Court IEEPA tariff refunds; CIT certifies importer class
events.why_it_matters: Class certification clears a path for importers to recover IEEPA tariffs struck down in February, a cash-flow positive for retailers but a fiscal cost.
events.what_to_watch: Refund timing, the size of claims and whether the administration appeals.

events.title: Google asks DC Circuit to overturn search monopoly remedies
events.why_it_matters: Google's appeal against the remedies forcing it to share search data with rivals could reshape the US search and default-payment landscape.
events.what_to_watch: DC Circuit scheduling and whether the Apple default-payments ban is stayed.

events.title: AHA Scientific Sessions 2026
events.why_it_matters: Late-breaking cardiovascular and obesity data at the year's largest heart meeting can move pharma, medtech and GLP-1 names.
events.what_to_watch: Late-breakers on obesity, heart failure and any surprise trial readouts.

events.title: SEMICON Europa 2026
events.why_it_matters: Europe's flagship semiconductor conference will focus on advanced packaging, fab management and the EU chip strategy amid export-control fragmentation.
events.what_to_watch: Capex commentary from ASML, Infineon and equipment makers; EU policy signals.

events.title: Atlantic hurricane season turns dormant into early November
events.why_it_matters: Forecasts show the Gulf and tropical Atlantic largely dormant into at least the first week of November, removing a seasonal supply-disruption premium.
events.what_to_watch: Any late-season named storm and Gulf oil/gas platform shut-ins.

events.title: China Evergrande liquidation and property downturn persist
events.why_it_matters: Evergrande's liquidation and a nearly 20% decline in property investment keep a drag on Chinese domestic demand and commodity imports.
events.what_to_watch: Property sales, developer defaults and any new PBOC housing stimulus.

events.title: US October ISM manufacturing and services PMIs
events.why_it_matters: Regional Fed surveys point to a rebound, with ISM manufacturing consensus around 54.7 after 54.5, keeping the soft-landing narrative intact.
events.what_to_watch: Prices-paid components and new orders for inflation and capex signals.

events.title: FDA PDUFA decision on Agios mitapivat for sickle cell disease
events.why_it_matters: A approval would validate Agios's hematology franchise; a rejection would hit sentiment for small-cap biotech ahead of year-end.
events.what_to_watch: Label scope and safety language.

top_risks: A hot September core PCE print on October 29 hardens the case for a December Fed hike, pushing 10-year yields above 5.1% and pressuring long-duration equities.
Iranian retaliation or a formal Hormuz closure after the US midterms could spike Brent above $120 and reignite global inflation.
The US shutdown persists past the election, cancelling more data (including October jobs) and creating a Fed policy blackout into December.
A contested or delayed midterm result, combined with a French-style political impasse, could widen credit spreads and hit the dollar.
The East/Gulf port strike spreads to LA/Long Beach on November 1, disrupting holiday-season inventories and lifting goods inflation.
top_opportunities: Microsoft's Azure beat and SK Hynix's memory super-cycle confirm AI infrastructure demand, supporting semis, memory and data-centre suppliers.
A shutdown-ending deal in the Senate would remove a growth overhang and likely spark a relief rally in cyclicals and small caps.
Apple's November 2 print with a new CEO could reset expectations for the hardware upgrade cycle and AI monetisation.
Anthropic's IPO roadshow could create a positive read-through for AI software and private-market valuations.
OPEC+ discipline and dormant hurricane season reduce near-term energy supply tail risks, supporting transport and consumer discretionary margins.
summary: Markets enter the final days before the US midterms with the Fed on hold but two dissents for a hike, the longest government shutdown on record, and a first-ever cancellation of October CPI. Mega-cap earnings are diverging sharply — Microsoft and memory names are strong while Alphabet sold off on AI capex doubts — and the Iran/Hormuz risk premium remains the biggest tail risk. The next two weeks are dominated by the November 3 election, the November 4 Treasury refunding, Apple and AI/semis earnings, and a data blackout that will make the December Fed decision unusually blind.
